name: PacketFence-VM
description: Installs PacketFence, the open source network access control (NAC) system, as a virtual machine in the Unraid VM tab. PacketFence itself does not run in Docker; this container is only the installer. It downloads the official PacketFence ZEN appliance (about 8 GB, MD5-checked), converts its VMware disk into an Unraid vdisk, creates the VM and starts it. Then the container stops. The VM is a normal Unraid VM: start, stop, edit and back it up in the VM tab. Running the container again never changes an existing VM. Needs: VMs enabled (Settings > VM Manager), 16 GB of free memory and 4 cores for the VM, about 40 GB free in the VM storage during the import (the vdisk is 200 GB thin-provisioned, about 21 GB used). After the start: open the VM's VNC console in the VM tab. The first network card gets its address by DHCP. Console login root / p@ck3tf3nc3 (change it). Then open https://VM-address:1443 and go through the configurator.

paths.name: VM storage
paths.description: Your VM storage (Settings > VM Manager > Default VM storage path). The vdisk goes to VM-name/vdisk1.img in here.

paths.name: Downloads
paths.description: Where the ZEN appliance zip is downloaded to. An existing PacketFence-ZEN-vVERSION.zip here or in the VM storage is used instead of downloading.

paths.name: libvirt
paths.description: libvirt socket, used to create the VM. Do not change.

paths.name: Docker socket
paths.description: Only used to read the host path of VM storage for the VM definition.

paths.name: VM icons
paths.description: Unraid's folder for custom VM icons; the PacketFence icon is copied here. Remove to use the Debian icon.

variables.name: VM name
variables.description: Name of the VM in the VM tab and of its folder in the VM storage. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'.

variables.name: PacketFence version
variables.description: latest, or a version with a ZEN appliance such as 15.2.0.

variables.name: CPU cores
variables.description: Virtual CPU cores. PacketFence asks for at least 4.

variables.name: Memory (GB)
variables.description: VM memory in GB. PacketFence asks for at least 16.

variables.name: Network
variables.description: Unraid bridge for the VM's network card: br0, br0.10 for VLAN 10, or vhost0. PacketFence's guide says to start with one card; a comma-separated list (br0,br0.10) adds more.

variables.name: MAC address
variables.description: Optional MAC for the first network card, for example when your DHCP server only serves known MACs. Empty = random (shown in the container log).

variables.name: VNC keyboard
variables.description: Keyboard layout of the VNC console, for example en-us, de, fr.

variables.name: Start VM
variables.description: Start the VM right after it is created.

variables.name: VM autostart
variables.description: Start the VM when the array starts (same as the Autostart switch in the VM tab).

variables.name: Keep download
variables.description: Keep the downloaded zip after the import (no deletes it).

variables.name: Source file
variables.description: Optional: your own .zip, .ova or .vmdk, as a container path (for example /downloads/PacketFence-ZEN-v15.2.0.zip), or a URL. Empty = official download.

variables.name: Vdisk bus
variables.description: virtio is fastest; the appliance boots from all three.

variables.name: VM storage host path
variables.description: Only needed without the Docker socket: the host path of VM storage, for example /mnt/user/domains.
